Additional comments:
questions.answer: it wasn't so straight forward to figure out what chances you had of getting into a course, how many you should apply for, considering risk of not getting in to some courses etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything worked through the online ufind portal, finding courses and their description. I had a lot of problems with accidently signing up for MA courses, which i was not allowed to follow, and then i didnt find out it was a MA course until the first day of class. It was a difficult portal to navigate in, but with attention and time it is doable.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus students admin was available several times per week for in person help or on the phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It worked out, but i had some trouble with filling out half my ECTS points with English language courses in my nominated field - so i ended up having to take a German course, which i failed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
In terms of relations, and getting to know people, you really have to say yes to everything that is offered in the beginning, because it stops very quickly.
Bureaucratically, you have to go to the municipality office in the district you are staying and register your residency within 3 days, or you can be fined! After that you have to go to the central office within a month, and register that you have sufficient funds via the Erasmus grant.
Academically, i would say try to take fewer seminars, and more lectures. The seminars often have bigger exams, like essays, and can in some cases involve data collection etc. Lectures are written exams, either multiple choice, written questions, or essay questions. However, lecture exams are often written in hand!

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Because i wanted to take my classes in English, i had to take classes from across semesters, so i also had some first semester introduction to sociological classics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The seminars are more independent, its often PHD students doing classes they themselves have formulated. So they are often are lot more interesting. Also i has one teacher who was a declared Marxist, which i doubt would be welcomed in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Guided Reading: Classics of Sociological Texts
- Gender Inequality from a Life Course Perspective
- Urban Sociology - Cities, territories, governance
-  Theoretical Traditions and Developments in Anthropology
-  Introduction to Urban Conflict
- New Critical Perspectives in Social and Cultural Anthropology
- Gesellschaftsdiagnosen

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Urban Conflict, with Ajin Tas was a very eye-opening course, introducing me to new and more global perspective's.
New Critical Perspectives in Social and Cultural Anthropology, with Mafe was also academically extremely awarding.
and Guided Reading: Classics of Sociological Texts with Pavel Pospech was just a joy - Pavel  is a very good teacher.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food culture, and the love of nice quality things! There are a lot of affordable really nice food and amazing restaurant options. In the supermarket the quality is really good, unlike Denmark where the main selling point has become discount. The Austrians expect quality, and i love them for that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to register your residency at the municipality office! Remember to register to more courses than you need, because you wont get into all of them, and be sure that the courses dont overlap - and remember to deregister for seminars you wont be following anyway before the deregistration period is over. And finally, you can register to take exams in lectures even if you didnt follow the course, and you can register to courses at any time during the semester - this means you can change if something is too boring or too difficult.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That my exams from vienna last all the way to the end of march - so its very stressful to be working on all that on the side of the BA project and other courses.
